name: RFA One
best_known_for: Germany's three-stage small launcher, stacked at SaxaVord in 2026 and not yet flown
credit: In development, never flown (no launch through 2026-11-25). Sources: Wikipedia RFA One (static-fire anomaly 2024-08-19, UK licence Jan 2025, 30 m, 2 m, 1,300 kg), ESA image caption (2.15 m, 500 kg to SSO), advanced-television.com (Nov 2026 slip to 2027), European Spaceflight (Jul 2026). RFA's own statement on the 2024 accident was not found. Source conflicts: diameter 2 m (Wikipedia; used, as the 30 m comes from the same page) against 2.15 m (ESA); payload to a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit 1,300 kg (Wikipedia) against 500 kg (ESA image caption, the most recent; used in the text). The 1,300 kg figure may be to LEO, not verified. Checked 2026-11-25.
